question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The politician used a/an __mild and indirect word__ to describe the controversial policy, in order to soften the blow.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Euphemism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"mild and indirect word"** refers to a way of describing something unpleasant or controversial in a more pleasant or less offensive manner. (मृदु और परोक्ष शब्द)
 
• **"Euphemism"** is the use of a mild or indirect word or expression to replace one considered to be too harsh, blunt, or offensive. (व्यंजना)
 
 
• **Example:** Using "passed away" instead of "died" is a common euphemism.
 
 
 
• Therefore, using a euphemism to describe the controversial policy softens the potential negative impact of the discussion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Euphemism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Oxymoron** (विरोधाभास): A figure of speech in which apparently contradictory terms appear in conjunction.
 
 
• **Example:** "Bitter sweet" is an example of an oxymoron.
 
 
 
• **Metaphor** (रूपक): A figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.
 
 
• **Example:** "Time is a thief" is a metaphor that suggests time stealthily takes away our moments.
 
 
 
• **Hyperbole** (अतिशयोक्ति): Exaggerated statements or claims not meant to be taken literally.
 
 
• **Example:** "I've told you a million times" is a hyperbole used for emphasis.
